confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on two web searches. One was an RBA exchange-rate search. The other was a single search of crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites (expatistan, citycost, traveltables and others). Those sites put a cappuccino at about €3–3.65, a 0.5 L local draft beer at about €3.9–4.1 and an inexpensive meal at about €12–15. For the three-course mid-range meal for two, the sources ranged from about €30 to about $42, so I chose a higher figure of about $58 to reflect July peak-season prices in Chania's tourist areas. I didn't search for cocktail or wine prices. I estimated those from typical Greek resort prices relative to beer, so they are less certain. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge of July peak season in Crete, not checked against booking sites. Hostel supply in Chania is thin, so the hostel anchors are especially uncertain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with other mid-sized Greek island tourist towns in peak season, such as Heraklion, Rethymno and Corfu Town. Chania costs a little more than mainland Greek cities and less than Mykonos or Santorini.
